newsitem.title: UK: BA sacks union boss after "fat cat" fight.
newsitem.headline: BA sacks union boss after "fat cat" fight.

text.p: British Airways Plc said Tuesday that the head of the airline's biggest cabin crew union was fired for assaulting another employee, following a dispute over allegations of being a "fat cat" union boss.

Mike Coleman, the branch secretary of the British Airlines Stewards and Stewardesses Association (BASSA) was accused of hitting Dave Fallon, an official with the smaller rival union Cabin Crew 89, after he caught Fallon handing out copies of a newspaper article about him to fellow workers at British Airway's London Heathrow headquarters.

A Daily Mirror story in January said Coleman earned more than 100,000 British pounds ($162,000) last year, making him Britain's highest paid union boss, despite representing only 9,000 people at British Airways.

Headlined "Brother Fat Cat," the article said Coleman had supplemented his 32,000 pounds salary ($51,000) from British Airways with 50,000 pounds ($81,000) in annual commissions on union membership subscriptions and 20,000 pounds ($32,000) in daily expense allowances.
"People have got a grudge but I have nothing to hide. I work hard for our members," Coleman was quoted as saying.
British Airways said Tuesday that Coleman had been dismissed as the result of a disciplinary hearing, and lost his appeal last Friday.
